newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Ex-Soviet teams dominate world cities' chess.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Soviet teams dominate world cities' chess.

text.p: The race for medals at the World Cities Chess Championship in Jakarta was all but decided on Sunday after a series of crushing wins for teams from the former Soviet Union.
The Ukrainian team from Donetsk increased its lead to 2.5 points by whitewashing the local hopes Depok Margonda in the ninth round.

A crowd of around 50 watched as, one by one, the grandmasters from Ukraine forced their international master opponents to resign. The final blow was the loss of Cerdas Barus to Aleksandr Shneider after four hours of fruitless defence.
Top seeds Moscow looked likely to be forced to settle for the silver medals, as their 3.5-0.5 demolition of Sydney was insufficient to keep pace with Donetsk.

But Moscow held a two point margin over its nearest rival for silver, Tashkent. Tashkent, who struggled for form until top player Aleksandr Nenashev arrived in Jakarta from Uzbekistan a few days ago, moved into clear third place for the first time.
Earlier, in round eight, Donetsk had little trouble disposing of lowly-ranked Rangoon. Only a draw by Rangoon's top player Zaw Win Lay against Igor Novikov prevented a 4-0 whitewash.
Moscow squeezed to a 2.5-1.5 victory over Tashkent thanks to a victory by its top-scoring player, Sergei Tiviakov.
The inaugural World Cities Championships, featuring 30 teams from 14 countries, conclude on Monday.
